item.text:
I treated your local prior as the baseline and did not re-fetch structured country-year facts already supplied there.

**Office, authority, constraints**
- Abiy Ahmed’s formal office in 2022 was Prime Minister of Ethiopia, not president. Under the Ethiopian constitution, the PM is the chief executive, chairs the Council of Ministers, and is commander-in-chief of the armed forces.
- His authority is real but not unilateral: the PM and cabinet are responsible to the House of Peoples’ Representatives, ministers are approved by the House, and emergency powers require parliamentary approval.
- In 2022 his room to maneuver was constrained by the ongoing northern war, federal/regional fragmentation, humanitarian pressure, and external mediation by the AU/IGAD/UN.

**Retained source set**
1. [Proclamation no. 1 Constitution of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia](https://www.lawethiopia.com/index.php/legislation/2445-proclamation-no-1?highlight=WyJjb2RlIiwiY3JpbWluYWwiLCJjaXZpbCIsImNvZGUiXQ%3D%3D) - LawEthiopia, constitutional text. Precise fact: the PM is chief executive, chair of the Council of Ministers, commander-in-chief, and responsible to the House; the cabinet may declare a state of emergency but must submit it for approval. Period fit: legal baseline for all 2022 judgments. Ruler attribution: direct formal authority and direct formal constraint. Limitations: static legal text, not performance evidence. Contrary points: parliamentary responsibility and emergency approval limit unilateral action.

2. [Government](https://ethiopianembassy.org/government/) - Embassy of Ethiopia. Precise fact: Ethiopia is described as a federal democracy headed by an executive PM; the page lists Dr. Abiy Ahmed as PM and the president as head of state. Period fit: office-definition cross-check. Ruler attribution: confirms office shape and current title. Limitations: present-day snapshot, not archival 2022 evidence. Contrary points: use the constitution for the legal baseline, not this summary alone.

3. [Ethiopia's parliament lifts state of emergency early](https://www.euronews.com/2022/02/16/us-ethiopia-conflict) - Reuters via Euronews, 16 Feb 2022. Precise fact: parliament ended the six-month state of emergency immediately; the emergency had allowed detention without charge and warrantless home searches. Period fit: key 2022 constraint reset. Ruler attribution: shows Abiy operating under legislative approval and managing political divisions. Limitations: wire summary, not the legal text itself. Contrary points: opposition argued the move was premature; the government said the law had caused more harm than benefit.

4. [IGAD Appreciate Announcement of Ethiopian Gov’t Humanitarian Truce](https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_34548) - Ethiopian News Agency, 25 Mar 2022. Precise fact: IGAD welcomed Ethiopia’s indefinite humanitarian ceasefire and the reciprocal Tigray announcement, saying it should improve humanitarian access and help address drought and food insecurity. Period fit: mid-year inflection point. Ruler attribution: captures the government’s own peace framing and its regional endorsement. Limitations: state-friendly framing, not independent fact-finding. Contrary points: does not test implementation or address alleged abuses. Note: this ENA page also exposes Amharic, Tigrinya, Afaan Oromoo, Af-Soomaali, Qafar Afa, French, and Arabic versions, so it is the best retained local-language family to follow.

5. [Factbox-Key points in Ethiopia's ceasefire agreement](https://www.euronews.com/2022/11/05/ethiopia-conflict-agreement) - Reuters via Euronews, 5 Nov 2022. Precise fact: the Pretoria deal called for a permanent cessation of hostilities, restoration of federal authority in Tigray, disarmament within 30 days, an interim administration, humanitarian access, and transitional justice; Eritrea and disputed-territory questions were left unresolved. Period fit: the decisive late-2022 turning point. Ruler attribution: shows Abiy’s government negotiating under external mediation and with unresolved constraints. Limitations: summary of a shared text, not implementation proof. Contrary points: the agreement itself leaves key issues open.

6. [Agreement for Lasting Peace through a Permanent Cessation of Hostilities between the Government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia and the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF)](https://peacemaker.un.org/en/node/10038) - UN Peacemaker, 2 Nov 2022. Precise fact: the official peace-agreement text is archived here. Period fit: primary legal record for the 2022 peace pivot. Ruler attribution: the Ethiopian government is a signing party. Limitations: it records commitments, not compliance. Contrary points: later implementation disputes and residual insecurity do not disappear because the agreement was signed.

7. [OHCHR-EHRC joint advisory note on Transitional Justice](https://ethiopia.un.org/en/212602-ohchr-ehrc-joint-advisory-note-transitional-justice) - UN Ethiopia / OHCHR / EHRC, 19 Dec 2022. Precise fact: the note welcomes the 2 Nov 2022 peace agreement, cites the requirement for a national transitional-justice policy, and says consultations ran across Afar, Amhara, Harar, Oromia, Somali, and Dire Dawa; planned Tigray consultations were postponed because fighting resumed in August. Period fit: strong inherited-conditions and post-agreement source. Ruler attribution: directly ties the state to the transitional-justice follow-through. Limitations: advisory and consultative, not adjudicative. Contrary points: it explicitly records that renewed fighting blocked fuller consultation.

8. [Annual Report 2022](https://www.unicef.org/ethiopia/reports/annual-report-2022) - UNICEF Ethiopia, April 2023. Precise fact: Ethiopia faced multiple emergencies in 2022, including conflict in Afar, Amhara, and Tigray, sporadic inter-ethnic conflict, and the worst drought in forty years in Afar, Oromia, and Somali; 29.7 million people needed humanitarian assistance. Period fit: strongest compact baseline for inherited conditions. Ruler attribution: countrywide welfare context, not personal credit or blame. Limitations: humanitarian and child-focused; not ruler-specific. Contrary points: it captures the operating environment rather than proving direct causation.

9. [“We Will Erase You from This Land”: Crimes Against Humanity and Ethnic Cleansing in Ethiopia’s Western Tigray Zone](https://www.hrw.org/report/2022/04/06/we-will-erase-you-land/crimes-against-humanity-and-ethnic-cleansing-ethiopias) - Amnesty International and Human Rights Watch, 6 Apr 2022. Precise fact: the report says Western Tigray abuses since November 2020 involved Amhara regional forces and local authorities, with the acquiescence and possible participation of Ethiopian federal forces, and that several hundred thousand Tigrayans were expelled. Period fit: critical for rights, territorial control, and security chapters. Ruler attribution: strongest adverse evidence in the retained set for federal responsibility concerns. Limitations: region-specific and conflict-specific. Contrary points: the government denied core allegations and access restrictions limited verification.

10. [Update: Federal government declares humanitarian truce in Tigray effective today; says move paves way for resolution of conflict](https://addisstandard.com/update-federal-government-declares-humanitarian-truce-in-tigray-effective-today-says-move-paves-way-for-resolution-of-conflict/) - Addis Standard, 24 Mar 2022. Precise fact: the independent local outlet reported the government’s declaration of an indefinite humanitarian truce and its stated goal of enabling aid and conflict resolution. Period fit: useful local independent confirmation of the March turning point. Ruler attribution: local press coverage of a federal decision. Limitations: reports a government statement, not field verification. Contrary points: later fighting showed the truce was fragile.

**Best source families by chapter**
- 1B: NTI / IAEA / Pelindaba Treaty plus SIPRI if a nuclear-baseline check is ever needed. For Abiy 2022, this remains a no-evidence shelf unless the question changes.
- 2B: Reuters, ENA, UN statements, UCDP/SIPRI for conflict and force context.
- 3B: HRW, Amnesty, EHRC/OHCHR, Addis Standard, UNICEF for violence, repression, and civilian harm.
- 4B: Constitution, embassy/government pages, Reuters, Addis Standard, ENA for office, institutions, elections, and political space.
- 5B: World Bank WDI/Maddison, IMF, UNICEF for scale and inherited economic conditions.
- 6B: UNICEF, WHO, UNDP for welfare, health, schooling, mortality, and drought stress.
- 7B: WGI, V-Dem, Transparency International, plus rights reporting where corruption is tied to coercion or capture.
- 8B: WGI, UN/OCHA, government budget and implementation reporting, Reuters, ENA for state capacity and delivery.

**Compact event map**
- 2 Nov 2021: state of emergency imposed amid the northern war.
- 15 Feb 2022: parliament lifts the state of emergency early.
- 24-25 Mar 2022: government announces an indefinite humanitarian truce.
- Apr 2022: rights groups publish major Western Tigray abuse findings.
- Aug 2022: fighting resumes in the north, disrupting consultations and services.
- 2 Nov 2022: Pretoria cessation-of-hostilities agreement signed.
- 19 Dec 2022: UN/EHRC note pushes transitional-justice follow-through.

**Chapter source plan**
- Use the constitution and embassy page for office/authority.
- Use Reuters plus Addis Standard/ENA for the 2022 sequence of emergency, truce, and peace process.
- Use UN Peacemaker and OHCHR-EHRC for the legal transition from war to implementation.
- Use HRW/Amnesty and UNICEF for the hardest inherited-condition and rights baselines.

If you want, I can turn this into a tighter evidence dossier format with one source per line and a chapter-by-chapter “what this source can and cannot support” grid.
